_comment: Template for DevToolBox's per-machine command mapping file.
This file itself is NOT read by DevToolBox — it is a copy-paste starting
point. To activate it, copy this file's *contents* into the real path
returned by platform::machine_commands_path() (see
aidd_docs/memory/architecture.md, 'Per-machine command resolution'):
- Linux:   $XDG_STATE_HOME/devtoolbox/machine-commands.json
(falls back to ~/.local/state/devtoolbox/machine-commands.json)
- Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\DevToolBox\machine-commands.json
This '_comment' key is not part of the schema DevToolBox expects (only
'machines' is read); it is silently ignored by the loader, so you may
keep it or delete it once you understand the shape below.
Shape: { "machines": { "<machine-id>": { "<command-id>": "<override string>" } } }
- <machine-id>: matched case-insensitively against platform::machine_id()
(the DEVTOOLBOX_MACHINE_ID env var if set, else the OS hostname, else
"unknown"). A disabled card in the app shows the exact machine id to
use for the current machine in its inline message.
- <command-id>: the 'id' field (not 'name') of a command in config.json
that has "machine_specific": true. A disabled card's inline message
also names the missing command id.
- <override string>: the literal launch string to use on that machine
instead of the command's default 'command' field — same format as
'command' (may itself be an '@python <script> [args...]' invocation).
Only machines/commands you list here are overridden; every other
machine-specific command on an unlisted machine renders disabled until
you add an entry for it.
